newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to offer 45 pct of Bank Handlowy late May.
newsitem.headline: Poland to offer 45 pct of Bank Handlowy late May.

text.p: Poland will offer 15 percent of its Bank Handlowy SA to domestic retail investors and 30 percent to Polish and foreign institutions in a public subscription starting in late May, the bank's head said on Wednesday.

"I can say now that the subscription will begin in late May," Cezary Stypulkowski told a news conference after the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) cleared all Bank Handlowy shares for public trade.
The commission said in a statement that 61.75 million out of Handlowy's 65 million shares would be put up for sale.

It said 45 percent of shares would be offered in subscription to retail and institutional investors, up to 42.86 percent offered to a group of selected international finacial institutions and 7.14 perecent of shares would be offered to Handlowy's employees.
The state treasury would retain five percent of shares.
The commission said it had also approved a plan to issue Global Depositary Receipts as a part of the public offering. @
Stypulkowski said the detailed offering timetable and other details would be published in an issue prospectus on May 12.
"I have reasons to believe that by the end of June, Bank Handlowy will be privatised," he said.
Shareholder: state treasury - 100 pct of shares
